overview: Host John Petrella interviewed School Committee Vice Chair Jenny Graham regarding the Medford High School project. The discussion covered the construction timeline, state reimbursement formulas, and the vision for a modernized campus that integrates vocational and pre-K programs.

items.title: Introduction and Guest Background
items.summary: John Petrella introduced Jenny Graham, who shared her personal history as a Medford resident, parent, and CEO of a consulting firm.

items.title: High School Project Timeline and Milestones
items.summary: Graham reported that the project entered the feasibility phase in 2024 following MSBA acceptance in late 2023. The committee is narrowing down design options from a broad list to a single selection by June.

items.title: Educational Scope and Site Utility
items.summary: The proposed project aims to serve as a community hub by consolidating vocational programs, pre-K classrooms, and administrative offices onto one campus. This plan is intended to alleviate overcrowding in Medford's elementary schools and provide modernized science labs and vocational spaces.

items.title: Operational Costs and Maintenance
items.summary: The committee discussed the high utility costs and facility failures of the current building, noting monthly energy bills of approximately $162,000. Graham stated that the cost to bring the existing building to code without educational improvements would be $438 million, which would receive no state reimbursement.

items.title: Project Budget and Financial Structure
items.summary: Graham explained that total project costs include construction, materials, and labor, while bond interest and tax calculations will be determined later. There are no anticipated provisions in the project budget for adjustments to teacher union contracts.

items.title: MSBA Reimbursement and Funding Formula
items.summary: The MSBA is currently reimbursing 53% of feasibility costs, with final construction reimbursement to be determined by community wealth factors and maintenance incentive points. The city is exploring a debt exclusion and potential revenue from other developments to offset the local funding burden.

items.title: Project Management and Design Team
items.summary: Medford has hired LeftField as the Owner's Project Manager and SMMA as the designer, both of which have experience building large-scale comprehensive schools. Graham emphasized the team's role in managing contractors and ensuring the project stays on schedule.

items.title: Design Selection Process
items.summary: A 25-member committee, including 15 voting members, is evaluating design options based on community feedback and long-term value. Graham noted that the group is using community forums and visual preference surveys to narrow down the nearly 30 initial design options.

subject: High School Building Project Timeline and Costs
